case_title.quote: Vinod Jaswantray Vyas (Dead) Through Lrs. v. The State of Gujarat
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.quote: tried the accused appellant Vinod Jaswantray Vyas... and his co-accused Chinubhai Govindbhai Patel
number_of_accused.reason: Two accused (A1 and A2) were tried together.

accused_gender.quote: the accused appellant Vinod Jaswantray Vyas... and altered his conviction
accused_gender.reason: Accused referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for either accused.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.quote: The accused appellant(A1) was posted as a Police Inspector at Amraiwadi Police Station
accused_occupation.reason: A1 was a Police Inspector; A2 was Superintendent of Police.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status of accused is not discussed.

previous_criminal_record.reason: Antecedents discussed concern the victim, not the accused; accused record is not stated.

victim_gender.quote: Jeeva had come to surrender at the police station along with his advocate
victim_gender.reason: Victim Jeeva is male, referred to as brother and with male pronouns.

victim_age.reason: No age for the victim Jeeva appears in the judgment.

victim_caste.reason: Victim's caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: Victim's religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Police officers holding the victim in custody (no prior relationship stated)
accused_victim_relationship.quote: The accused appellant(A1) was posted as a Police Inspector at Amraiwadi Police Station
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Accused were police officers with custodial control over the victim, not strangers.

offence_category.correct_value: Murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.114); High Court altered to culpable homicide under s.304 Part I
offence_category.quote: the offence punishable under Section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860 to one under Section 304 Part I IPC
offence_category.reason: Trial charge was murder under s.302; culpable homicide applies only to the High Court's altered conviction.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s.302 r/w s.114; s.304 Part I (High Court)
statutory_provisions.quote: for the offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 114 IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Section 302 is right, but s.34 and Arms Act s.27 are not in the judgment; s.114 is omitted.

weapon.quote: assaulted Jeeva with fists and sticks in the confines of the police station
weapon.reason: The judgment identifies fists and sticks as the weapons used.

evidence_type.correct_value: Eyewitness and medical evidence; circumstantial evidence not expressly identified
evidence_type.quote: formidable evidence of the Medical Jurist (PW-9) which totally discredits the version of the so called eyewitnesses
evidence_type.reason: Medical and eyewitness evidence are central; circumstantial evidence is not identified as a category.

confession.reason: No confession by the accused is mentioned in the judgment.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Aggravating circumstances are not discussed in the judgment.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: Mitigating circumstances are not discussed in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.quote: proceeded to convict both the accused for the above offences and sentenced them to imprisonment for life
trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted under s.302 r/w 114 and sentenced to life imprisonment.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Affirmed guilt; s.302 altered to s.304 Part I; eight years RI and Rs 50,000 compensation
high_court_outcome.quote: the offence was toned down from Section 302 IPC to offence under Section 304 Part I IPC
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court did act: it altered the offence and modified the sentence.

final_outcome.quote: both accused i.e. Vinod Jaswantray Vyas(A1)(since deceased) and Chinubhai Govindbhai Patel(A2)(since deceased) are acquitted of the charges

offence_finally_established.quote: the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of both the accused persons
offence_finally_established.reason: No offence was finally established given the acquittal.

imprisonment_type.quote: both the accused... are acquitted of the charges
imprisonment_type.reason: No final imprisonment, since both accused were acquitted.

imprisonment_years.reason: No final imprisonment term applies after acquittal.

fine_rs.reason: No final fine applies after acquittal; trial-court fine was set aside.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Neutral facts should omit the outcome; remove 'leading to the acquittal of the accused'
neutral_facts.quote: Both the accused i.e. Vinod Jaswantray Vyas(A1)(since deceased) and Chinubhai Govindbhai Patel(A2)(since deceased) are acquitted
neutral_facts.reason: Neutral facts reveal the court outcome by stating the acquittal.

offence_severity.correct_value: Maximum: life imprisonment (trial sentence); no minimum stated
offence_severity.quote: sentenced them to imprisonment for life and fine of Rs. 25,000/- each
offence_severity.reason: Life imprisonment is supported; the 6-year minimum is not in the judgment.

attempt_completion.quote: rushed to the civil hospital in the early hours of 12th June, 1992, where the doctors declared him dead
attempt_completion.reason: Offence resulted in the victim's death, so it is completed.

physical_harm.quote: causing multiple injuries all over his body due to which he became unconscious
physical_harm.reason: Multiple external and internal injuries, including fractures, leading to death, are described.

number_of_offences.correct_value: One offence (s.302 r/w s.114) charged against both accused
number_of_offences.quote: charges were framed by the trial Court against both the accused for the offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 114 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Only one offence was charged against both accused, not two.

financial_property_loss.correct_value: Not stated; High Court directed Rs 50,000 compensation to the heirs
financial_property_loss.quote: he shall pay a compensation of Rs. 50,000/- to the heirs of the deceased
financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss is stated, but a compensation order to heirs exists.

premeditation_planning.reason: Premeditation or planning is not discussed in the judgment.

motive.quote: The theory of motive attributed by the prosecution witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) to the accused A1 and A2 is also not palpable

key_evidence_accepted.quote: there is formidable evidence of the Medical Jurist (PW-9) which totally discredits the version of the so called eyewitnesses
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court relied on the Medical Jurist's evidence over the eyewitnesses.

witness_credibility.correct_value: PW-1 and PW-2 held to show unnatural conduct; PW-3 discredited for contradictions, omissions and infirmities
witness_credibility.quote: This pertinent omission in failing to inform their advocate about the custodial torture... casting a doubt on the truthfulness of their version
witness_credibility.reason: Unnatural-conduct finding applies to PW-1 and PW-2; PW-3 was rejected for infirmities, not unnatural conduct.

post_offence_conduct.reason: No accused post-offence conduct is discussed; only the sisters' complaint delay is noted.

custody_duration.quote: Next evening i.e. on 11th June, 1992, Jeeva was produced before the jurisdictional Magistrate, who remanded him to judicial custody
custody_duration.reason: Remand to judicial custody on 11 June and death on 12 June are supported.

bail_history.quote: the sentence awarded to the accused appellant(A1) was suspended vide order dated 6th June, 2017 and he was directed to be released on bail
bail_history.reason: Suspension of sentence and bail order are supported; A1's death is also stated.

trial_duration.quote: vide judgment dated 4th March, 1997... common judgment dated 13th February, 2017
trial_duration.reason: Offence, trial, High Court and Supreme Court dates are supported.

legal_representation.quote: Harin P. Raval, Sr. Adv., Anando Mukherjee, Ms. Ekta Bharati... Advs. for the Appellants.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names match the appearances section.

investigation_status.correct_value: Complaint registered as Criminal Case No. 1920 of 1993 after cognizance; trial completed; no charge sheet mentioned
investigation_status.quote: Cognizance was taken for the offence punishable under Section 302 IPC and the complaint came to be registered as Criminal Case No. 1920 of 1993
investigation_status.reason: Case registration and trial are supported; a charge sheet is not mentioned.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Non-examination of advocate Patanwadia, Anna Dorai and Meena; no prison-record investigation; delayed complaint
procedural_irregularity.quote: advocate Shri Patanwadia was not examined in evidence in support of the prosecution case
procedural_irregularity.reason: The judgment notes several investigative and examination lapses.

appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, High Court alteration and Supreme Court acquittal of both match the judgment.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Witnesses had no reason to falsely implicate; telegram was prompt; no delay; accused influenced the investigation
prosecution_argument.quote: the witnesses, Selvin Prabhakar(PW-1), Dhanlakshmi Vaiyapuri(PW-2) had no reason so as to falsely implicate the accused appellant
prosecution_argument.reason: Delay and lack of motive were defence points; the prosecution argued reliability and prompt telegram.

defence_argument.correct_value: Fresh injuries show assault in Sabarmati jail; eyewitnesses unreliable; delay, no motive, stairs-climbing impossibility also argued
defence_argument.quote: clearly Jeeva(deceased) had been assaulted at the Sabarmati Central jail and a totally false case has been foisted
defence_argument.reason: Jail-assault theory and eyewitness doubts are supported; delay, motive and stairs arguments are omitted.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Ocular evidence generally takes precedence; medical opinion prevails only where contradiction completely demolishes eyewitness version
legal_principle_applied.quote: generally, the evidence of the eyewitnesses should be given precedence. However, where the contradiction is so prominent
legal_principle_applied.reason: The value states medical precedence as the rule; the judgment gives eyewitnesses precedence generally, with an exception.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Also relied on Lahu Kamlakar Patil, Shivasharanappa, Narendrasinh Keshubhai Zala, Harvinder Singh, Chunthuram
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Sait Tarajee Khimchand and Others v. Yelamarti Satyam alias Satteyya
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Three cases listed correctly, but several others relied on for unnatural conduct are omitted.

sentencing_rationale.reason: No sentencing rationale applies since the accused were acquitted.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors are discussed by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: No aggravating factors are discussed by the court.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: High Court directed Rs 50,000 compensation to the heirs of the deceased
other_sentence_order.quote: he shall pay a compensation of Rs. 50,000/- to the heirs of the deceased
other_sentence_order.reason: The High Court ordered compensation to heirs, so 'None' is wrong.
